claim: GroupsJSONField sets default="{}" (a string), and DRF returns field defaults without to_internal_value, so an omitted `groups` sends the string "{}" to Rust, failing deserialization and producing HTTP 500 on every request that omits groups.
raw: #1 Critical: `groups` defaults to the string `"{}"`, so every request that omits it fails with HTTP 500. FeatureFlagTestEvaluationRequestSerializer.groups = GroupsJSONField(required=False), and GroupsJSONField.__init__ does kwargs.setdefault("default", "{}"). DRF returns a field default straight from get_default() without running to_internal_value, so validated_data["groups"] is the string "{}". `or {}` does not catch it — "{}" is truthy. get_flags_from_service puts the string into the JSON body; Rust FlagRequest.groups is Option<HashMap<String, Value>> so serde_json::from_value fails -> 400 -> raise_for_status -> HTTP 500. The sibling my_flags action in the same file already carries the exact guard this omits.

claim: The override payload built with model_to_dict returns a raw datetime for last_called_at and Dashboard model instances for the analytics_dashboards m2m, so json.dumps raises TypeError outside the local try and the endpoint returns HTTP 500 for any flag with traffic.
raw: #2 Critical: `model_to_dict` emits non-JSON-serializable values, so historical evaluation 500s for any flag with traffic. Only created_at/updated_at are isoformatted. model_to_dict also returns last_called_at (DateTimeField, editable, raw datetime) and analytics_dashboards (ManyToManyField, not in exclude, list of Dashboard instances). The TypeError is raised by requests' json=payload inside get_flags_from_service at :3539 — outside the local try but inside the outer try, landing in the blanket handler at :3612 -> HTTP 500. last_called_at is populated by a scheduled task every 30 minutes. The codebase already has the correct exclusion list (RECONSTRUCTABLE_FIELDS / field_exclusions["FeatureFlag"]).

claim: override_flags_definitions and only_use_override_person_properties are accepted ungated on the public /flags endpoint (only detailed_analysis got the is_internal_request gate), letting a holder of the public project token substitute flag definitions and use conditions as a property-inference oracle.
raw: #3 Critical: `override_flags_definitions` and `only_use_override_person_properties` are ungated on the public `/flags` endpoint. Only detailed_analysis is gated by is_internal_request; only_use_override_person_properties is passed ungated and request.override_flags_definitions is passed unconditionally into fetch_and_filter, which replaces the DB definition wholesale (*flag = override_flag). /flags authenticates with the team's public, client-embeddable project API token. Consequences: property-inference oracle over arbitrary distinct_ids; forced flag results including disabled/soft-deleted flags; property suppression flips negated operators (is_not, not_icontains, not_icontains_multi, not_regex, is_not_set return true).

claim: Adding only_use_override_person_properties to the early return short-circuits prepare_flag_evaluation_state, the sole caller of set_cohorts and group preparation, so cohort and group conditions silently evaluate as false for every timestamped evaluation.
raw: #4 High: `only_use_override_person_properties` skips *all* DB preparation, so cohort and group conditions silently evaluate as false. prepare_flag_evaluation_state is the sole caller of set_cohorts and also does group-type mapping and group-property preparation; short-circuiting leaves flag_evaluation_state.cohorts None and evaluate_cohort_filters falls back to an empty map. Django sends only_use_override_person_properties=True for every timestamped evaluation, so a cohort- or group-targeted flag that was genuinely ON is reported OFF with reason: no_condition_match, failed: false.

claim: skip_writes is computed from the raw ungated FlagsQueryParams rather than the post-gate values, so a public-token caller sending ?detailed_analysis=true silently disables experience-continuity hash-key persistence.
raw: #5 High: `skip_writes` is derived from the *ungated* query params, bypassing the gate that does exist. skip_writes: detailed_analysis.unwrap_or(false) || only_use_override_person_properties.unwrap_or(false) || *state.config.skip_writes uses raw FlagsQueryParams values, not the post-gate ones. skip_writes suppresses set_feature_flag_hash_key_overrides — the only DB write in the evaluation path. The gate protects the response but not the behavioral side effect.

claim: The historical rebuild copies only five kwargs plus filters from the reconstruction dict, so reconstructable fields like bucketing_identifier, ensure_experience_continuity and evaluation_runtime silently revert to Django defaults and bucketing differs from what users actually received.
raw: #6 High: Historical reconstruction discards most reconstructed fields, so bucketing reverts to model defaults. reconstruct_flag_at_timestamp returns every field in RECONSTRUCTABLE_FIELDS (including bucketing_identifier, ensure_experience_continuity, evaluation_runtime, is_remote_configuration, has_encrypted_payloads) but the rebuild copies five kwargs plus filters. Everything else becomes the Django field default. get_bucketing_identifier() selects the hash input from bucketing_identifier, so a flag that historically bucketed on device_id is re-hashed on distinct_id, landing the user in a different rollout bucket, with no warning.

claim: build_condition_analysis is a second matching implementation that evaluates every filter as a plain person property, so cohort, flag-dependency and group-property filters are reported as not matched while `enabled` on the same object says the flag matched.
raw: #7 High: The condition analysis is a second matching implementation and contradicts the real evaluator. build_condition_analysis does match_property(property, props, false).unwrap_or(false) against merged person properties only, while the canonical is_condition_match dispatches three ways (flag dependency, cohort batch evaluation, person OR group properties). It even classifies PropertyType::Cohort and PropertyType::Flag in type_str and then matches them as plain person properties, returning matched: false with explanations like "Property 'id' does not equal 5". Group-property filters fail the same way. Two matching implementations for one semantics will drift.

claim: rollout_excluded requires is_zero_rollout on every branch, so an ordinary partial-rollout exclusion (e.g. 50%) is reported false and gets the wrong explanation; and `matched` means all-properties-matched while the DRF help_text documents it as the condition that matched.
raw: #8 High: `rollout_excluded` requires a zero rollout, so the ordinary partial-rollout exclusion is mislabeled. is_zero_rollout = rollout_percentage == 0.0 is required on every branch that can set this_condition_rollout_excluded, including the branch where flag_match.condition_index already identifies the excluded condition. But check_rollout returns OutOfRolloutBound for any percentage below 100 whose hash falls outside the bucket, so for a 50% rollout rollout_excluded is false and the explanation falls through to the wrong branch. Second half: matched: all_properties_matched contradicts the DRF help_text "Whether this condition was the one that matched".

claim: Two paths discard the reconstructed override (Python except sets override_definitions = None; Rust logs a warn and keeps the DB flag) while the response still presents a historical answer with no field distinguishing it, and is_historical is never copied into the response.
raw: #9 High: A dropped override silently reports a present-day evaluation as historical. Python: except Exception -> logging.exception, override_definitions = None; evaluation proceeds against the current flag. Rust: Err(e) => tracing::warn!("Failed to parse override definition for flag ...") keeps the DB flag. In both cases the caller gets HTTP 200 carrying person_properties reconstructed at the timestamp and a result computed from today's conditions. The response serializer's seven fields distinguish neither case, and is_historical is read into reconstructed_flag_data and never copied into the response.

claim: The action requires only feature_flag:read but always returns the caller-chosen person's full property dictionary, so a feature-flag-scoped API key can enumerate arbitrary persons' PII; the sibling person endpoint returning the same data requires person:read.
raw: #10 High: `feature_flag:read` is enough to read any person's properties. The action is declared @action(methods=["POST"], detail=True, required_scopes=["feature_flag:read"]) but its response always includes the target person's full property dictionary — person.properties on the no-timestamp path and the reconstructed ClickHouse map otherwise — plus the per-property actual_value echo. Because distinct_id is caller-supplied, an API key scoped only to feature flags can enumerate arbitrary persons' properties across the team. The sibling posthog/api/person.py:1358 properties_at_time requires person:read.

claim: Removing the return_debug_info parameter and the isinstance timestamp guard breaks an existing caller in person.py (TypeError on unexpected keyword) and an existing test that asserts the removed ValueError message, introducing CI breakage.
raw: #11 High: `build_person_properties_at_time`'s signature change breaks an existing caller and an existing test. posthog/api/person.py:1443-1452 still calls build_person_properties_at_time(..., return_debug_info=True) and casts to a 4-tuple -> TypeError: unexpected keyword argument (behind if debug and settings.DEBUG). posthog/models/person/test/test_point_in_time_properties.py:41 asserts "timestamp must be a datetime object"; with the guard gone a non-datetime raises AttributeError from timestamp.astimezone(UTC) instead of ValueError, so this existing test fails.

claim: PropertyAnalysis.value is declared serializers.JSONField without allow_null while Rust emits JSON null for valueless filters (is_set/is_not_set), so response validation with raise_exception=True converts a successful evaluation into HTTP 500.
raw: #12 Medium: `PropertyAnalysis.value` is nullable in Rust but not in the serializer, turning a valid response into a 500. Rust emits value: property.value.clone().unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null), documented as the normal case for is_set / is_not_set filters. The serializer declares value = serializers.JSONField(...) with no allow_null, while the sibling actual_value does set it. Reproduced: value=None valid? False. Because the response serializer is validated with is_valid(raise_exception=True) inside the blanket except Exception, a single valueless property filter yields HTTP 500. Latent only because #15 keeps conditions empty today.

claim: The endpoint reads only flags[key]["enabled"] and never inspects failed, errorsWhileComputingFlags or quotaLimited, so four distinct failure modes collapse into an authoritative-looking 200 with result: false.
raw: #13 Medium: The endpoint never inspects the Rust failure signals, so four failure modes look like "flag was off". The action reads flags[key]["enabled"] and never checks flag_result["failed"], rust_response["errorsWhileComputingFlags"], or rust_response["quotaLimited"]. Four failures collapse into a 200 with result: false: override parse failure (warn only), team quota-limited (empty flags map -> flag_not_found), evaluation errored (enabled: false, failed: true), filtered by runtime/tag/survey rules (absent -> flag_not_found). failed itself is never exposed.

claim: Historical person properties are reconstructed from $set events only ($set_once handled only when event_name == "$set_once", $unset never), and the new composition with only_use_override_person_properties makes that partial reconstruction the entire property universe for evaluation.
raw: #14 Medium: Historical person properties are reconstructed from `$set` events only, then made authoritative. The merge loop applies $set from any event, applies $set_once only when event_name == "$set_once", and never handles $unset. The merge logic is pre-existing; what is new is the composition — the caller passes only_use_override_person_properties=timestamp is not None and get_person_properties then starts from an empty map. Because match_property is called with partial_props = false, an absent key makes is_not_set and not_icontains return Ok(true), so missing data reads as a positive match.

claim: INTERNAL_REQUEST_TOKEN is defined nowhere (no settings entry, no env template, no docs), so is_internal_request returns false, detailed_analysis is forced off and the endpoint returns conditions: [] indistinguishable from a flag with no conditions, while record_usage still bills the customer.
raw: #15 Medium: `INTERNAL_REQUEST_TOKEN` is defined nowhere, so the headline feature silently returns nothing. A repo-wide grep returns exactly two hits (config.rs:611 envconfig, feature_flag.py:3547 os.getenv). No posthog/settings entry, no compose/chart/env template, no documentation, nothing enforcing that the two services agree. If unset or mismatched, is_internal_request returns false, mod.rs:218 forces detailed_analysis to Some(false), FlagDetails.conditions is omitted and the Django or-chain falls through to []. HTTP 200 with conditions: [] is indistinguishable from a flag with no conditions. Simultaneously record_usage does not skip, so internal test evaluations are billed. The os.getenv call also bypasses the module's settings convention.

claim: flag_was_deleted is tracked only inside the `version_after is not None` guard, so a version-less `deleted` activity-log entry (as produced by bulk_delete) is skipped and a bulk-deleted flag is reported as alive at timestamps after deletion.
raw: #16 Medium: Version-less `deleted` entries are skipped, so a bulk-deleted flag is reported as alive. The docstring promises a flag is non-existent if it was soft-deleted at or before the timestamp, but deletion is tracked only inside `if version_after is not None`. FeatureFlagViewSet.bulk_delete logs activity="deleted" with Detail(changes=[], name=old_key) while updating via queryset.update(...) / bulk_update, neither of which touches version. Neither new test covers this combination. Validator located a concrete reachable path; severity raised from Low.

claim: The ClickHouse reconstruction query has no lower timestamp bound, no LIMIT and no row/byte/memory cap, is issued twice per request, and the new action declares no throttle_classes unlike the sibling PersonViewSet action calling the same function.
raw: #17 Medium: Unbounded ClickHouse scans, run twice, with a weaker throttle than the sibling caller of the same function. No lower timestamp bound, no LIMIT, sync_execute passed only max_execution_time which bounds wall clock, not rows or memory. The events ORDER BY puts distinct_id behind a disjunctive event predicate that defeats prefix pruning. Both person_existed_at_timestamp and build_person_properties_at_time are issued per request over the same range. The action declares no throttle_classes, whereas PersonViewSet.get_throttles() applies ClickHouseBurstRateThrottle to the sibling properties_at_time action calling the same function. The unbounded query shape itself is pre-existing; what is new is exposing it through a second, less protected endpoint.

claim: The override loop emits up to four tracing::info!/warn! lines per map entry with no cap on override_defs.len(), interpolating attacker-controlled keys and dumping the team's full flag.filters, and does an O(N*M) linear rescan plus deep clone per entry.
raw: #18 Medium: The override loop logs per entry at INFO, dumping flag filters, unbounded by request size. override_defs is an unbounded HashMap and axum's default 2 MB body limit is not overridden, so a body of minimal entries yields on the order of 10^5 attacker-controlled log lines per request. Lines 156 and 185 interpolate the raw attacker-controlled map key, which may contain newlines. Line 159 dumps the team's complete flag.filters via {:?} — cohort ids, property keys, email allowlists — into INFO logs. Each iteration does a full linear scan of flags plus a deep override_def.clone(), O(N*M). Local convention drift: the sibling filtering summary uses tracing::debug! gated by tracing::enabled!.

claim: operator strings are produced with format!("{:?}", op).to_lowercase(), bypassing the serde rename_all = "snake_case" on OperatorType, so the API emits noticontains/isnotset/notregex instead of PostHog's operator vocabulary.
raw: #19 Medium: `operator` strings come from Rust `Debug`, diverging from PostHog's operator vocabulary. operator: format!("{:?}", op).to_lowercase() bypasses #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] on OperatorType. Emitted values are noticontains, isnotset, notregex, semvergt, isdateafter — not not_icontains, is_not_set, not_regex. That file carries an explicit "Keep in sync with FEATURE_FLAG_SUPPORTED_OPERATORS" standard. Renaming a variant silently changes a public API string, with no serde attribute or test to catch it. The explanation_placeholder match also falls through to "does not match" for semver, date, *_multi and flag_evaluates_to operators.

claim: The diff adds a ~230-line DRF action with at least seven branches and a ~190-line Rust analysis function with no tests: test_feature_flag.py has zero references to test_evaluation and every Rust test change is mechanical struct-literal padding, so build_condition_analysis is never executed.
raw: #20 Medium: No tests for the new endpoint or the new Rust analysis function. No test file for the feature-flag API viewset appears in the changeset — posthog/api/test/test_feature_flag.py has zero references to test_evaluation — and every Rust test change in the diff is mechanical struct-literal padding (detailed_analysis: false, only_use_override_person_properties: false, conditions: None); no test sets any of them to true/Some(...), so build_condition_analysis is never executed by a test. This gap is directly why findings #1, #2, #7, #8 and #12 are in this report.

claim: is_internal_request compares against a single global unscoped env token with no per-team binding, expiry or rotation path, granting billing exemption and detailed_analysis for any team on the same public router.
raw: #21 Medium: The internal token is a single global unscoped secret granting billing exemption on every tenant. is_internal_request compares against one global Option<String> with no per-team field and never looks at the team being evaluated. A match causes record_usage to return early for whatever team_id the caller supplied and grants detailed_analysis for any team. /flags sits on the same public router as all customer SDK traffic, with no separate internal-only listener, port, or team allowlist. No expiry, key id, or rotation path. The repo has a mature per-team credential system (TokenAuthData) which this path does not use.

claim: hasattr(person, "distinct_ids") is always True because distinct_ids is a plain property, so the ORM fallback is unreachable, the hasattr check doubles the DB query, the comments invert reality, and except Exception: raise is a no-op.
raw: #22 Low: Unreachable `hasattr` branch, a doubled DB query, and a no-op `try`/`except`. Person.distinct_ids is a plain @property so hasattr is always True and the ORM fallback branch is unreachable; the comments invert reality. hasattr executes the property (running its PersonDistinctId query) and discards the result, then person.distinct_ids runs it again — two queries where the previous one-liner did one. The dead fallback omits .order_by("id") and feature_flag.py:3430 uses distinct_ids[0] for bucketing, so order is result-affecting. except Exception: raise is a no-op that reads as deliberate error handling while the docstring still advertises the removed wrapping.

claim: The four-way `or` chain probing for conditions in several response locations tests shapes the Rust producer cannot emit, and masks the real failure mode by making an empty conditions list indistinguishable from an absent field.
raw: #23 Low: Four-way `or` chain probes response shapes the producer cannot emit. Only the first candidate exists: FlagDetails has no rename_all, its new field is conditions, and neither FlagDetails nor FlagsResponse has an analysis member or a top-level conditions. The comment asserts uncertainty about a contract fully determined by code in this same repository. It also masks the real failure mode: because [] or ... falls through, a genuinely empty conditions list is indistinguishable from "field absent" — exactly the #15 case. .get("analysis", {}).get(...) would additionally raise AttributeError if analysis were ever non-dict.

claim: match_property(...).unwrap_or(false) discards Err, so a numeric comparison that could not be performed (unparseable actual value) is explained as a definite negated comparison result.
raw: #24 Low: A comparison that could not be performed is reported as a definite comparison result. match_property(property, props, false).unwrap_or(false) discards the Err variant. Gt/Gte/Lt/Lte return Err(FlagMatchingError::ValidationError(...)) when the actual value cannot be parsed as a number. For key age, operator Lte, filter value 30, actual value "not-a-number", the explanation becomes "Property 'age' > 30" — a specific negated comparison asserted as fact when no comparison happened. Narrowed: the matched: false boolean is correct because the canonical evaluator uses the identical pattern; only the prose is wrong.

claim: test_evaluation maps VersionNotFound and VersionHistoryIncomplete to HTTP 400 while returning 404 for person-not-found a few lines apart, giving two analogous "not present at the requested point" cases different semantics (and diverging from the sibling versions action's 404/422).
raw: #25 Low: Inconsistent error status codes for "not found at the requested point". test_evaluation maps both VersionNotFound and VersionHistoryIncomplete to HTTP 400, while the sibling versions action in the same viewset maps the same exception types to 404 and 422. Corrected framing: the cross-action comparison is weaker than it looks (path segment vs request body), and the {"error": ...} body key is the dominant convention in this file. The stronger self-contained point is inside the new action: 404 for person-not-found but 400 for flag-not-existing-at-timestamp, two analogous cases given different semantics a few lines apart.

claim: The internal bearer token is compared with String PartialEq (length check plus early-exit memcmp) rather than a constant-time primitive, in principle leaking a byte-position timing oracle.
raw: #26 Low: Non-constant-time comparison of the internal bearer token. auth_token == *internal_token uses String/str PartialEq — a length check plus early-exit memcmp — rather than a constant-time primitive. Assessed honestly: is_internal_request runs inside a pipeline dominated by JSON decoding, Postgres/Redis team verification and flag/cohort evaluation, so the sub-microsecond signal is buried under network jitter and multi-millisecond I/O. Theoretical rather than practically actionable — hence Low, not the finder's High. Fix: subtle::ConstantTimeEq or ring::constant_time::verify_slices_are_equal.
